application: Source-run Electron 44.7.2, production UI, disposable SQLite profile/project on Xvfb with background throttling disabled
scope: Observed dedicated language-worker isolates, not whole-app RAM, renderer retained documents, process RSS or inference memory. No garbage collection was forced.

secondExpiry.scope: Worker isolates only; no GC forced. Not whole-app RAM or a before/after savings estimate.

secondRecreation.scope: Worker isolates only; no GC forced. Not whole-app RAM or a before/after savings estimate.

firstExpiryObservation.note: Samples bracket expiry; they do not measure the exact 60-second deadline or collection latency.

checks.readmePreview: No dedicated worker target before a JSON file opened.
checks.workerReuse: The same worker target served sequential JSON document visits before its first expiry.
checks.dirtyDraft: A trailing-space edit remained unsaved and unchanged after expiry.
checks.undoRedo: Undo restored the exact original draft and cleared its dirty marker; redo restored the trailing space and dirty marker after worker recreation.
checks.diagnostics: After recreation, adding ! produced one JSON lint range and one gutter marker; undo removed the error.
checks.secondCycle: A second idle check found no workers; undo then restored original text, a clean dirty marker and zero lint errors with a third distinct worker target.

fullRegression.note: Full suite finished with the initial 9 worker tests. The expanded 12-test worker suite then passed separately.

limits: Formatter protocol and lifecycle covered by the shared client tests; native editor formatting normally uses the host formatter, so no native browser-formatter memory saving is claimed.
Worker heap samples include parser/modules/cache and transient allocations; they are not a retained-live-object comparison.
No packaged builds or macOS/Windows runtime measurements. Cold-start and rapid-typing latency still need workload profiling.
